title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 26
paragraphs: The Issedonians are said to have these customs. When a man's father is dead, all the relatives bring cattle to the house, and having slaughtered them and cut up the flesh, they also cut up the dead body of their host's father, and mixing all the flesh together they set out a banquet. His skull, however, they strip of flesh, clean out, and then gild over; and after that they treat it as a sacred object and perform great sacrifices for the dead man every year. This each son does for his father, just as the Hellenes keep the day of memorial for the dead. In other respects, too, this people is said to live righteously, and their women have equal rights with the men.
